summary: Stiletto Ridge's gabled L-4 cab, dated 1931, was believed burned in 1952; only a fire finder post, rock steps and a wind break remain in North Cascades National Park.

facts.status_note: Cab gone; dated 1931 to 1952 by FireLookout.com and believed burned in 1952 per Will Hite; only the fire finder post, rock steps and a rock wall wind break remain

access.note: Reached by a hike from the Bridge Creek Trailhead on Highway 20; the site is inside North Cascades National Park; Will Hite says it is easily accessible from the highway

visit.trail_note: Hike from the Bridge Creek Trailhead at 4,540 feet on Highway 20 to the site; the Stiletto Peak Trail climbs to the lookout site

events.note: Forest guard Kenneth Carmody sent to the station for the summer; Will Hite thinks there was probably only a camp and firefinder stand
Gabled L-4 cab dated to 1931 by the register and FireLookout.com; Will Hite says it was said to be built that year
Panorama photos taken from the site; Forest Lookouts dates them to September 9, 1934, Will Hite says they were taken from the roof
Register says a photo likely shows the cab being prepared for burning in 1952; Will Hite says it is believed to have been burned; Forest Lookouts lists it only as removed
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on October 28, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Will Hite say the cab was burned or prepared for burning around 1952; the Forest Lookouts page lists it only as removed. The story reports both.
The register and FireLookout.com place the site in the Wenatchee National Forest; the Forest Lookouts page names the Chelan National Forest. The sources do not reconcile the names.

notes_for_editor: Brief kind is ground: there is no tower, only a cab (later a site with rock features). The 1930 newspaper spells the peak Stilleto. The forest name conflict (Chelan vs Wenatchee) is unresolved in the sources. The Will Hite photo caption says 2025 but the page gives no text date. No new photos found. Brief status gone and FFLOS date confirmed; no corrections proposed.
